articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A six-year-old girl was allegedly assaulted by an eight-year-old classmate in a classroom in Panchkula, with CCTV footage capturing the attack. The incident raises concerns about school safety, supervision, and the influence of violent video games on children

The school’s auto-rickshaw arrived at its usual time around noon on October 28. Homemaker Aarti (name changed to protect privacy) took a quick, reassuring look at her six-year-old daughter’s uniform and schoolbag before waving her off with a smile. However, at 3:30 p.m., when the auto-rickshaw driver went to pick her up from her school in Haryana ’s Panchkula district, the girl was nowhere to be found. Her bag was kept at the school’s reception area.

The driver informed her family, who live just five minutes away from the school, and her father came rushing. As he called out her name, his voice grew louder with every frantic step towards the school building. He asked the teachers about his daughter’s whereabouts, and they joined him in his search. Soon, a boy approached him, asked his daughter’s name and confirmed whether he was looking for her. articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet PM Modi in New Delhi this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize ceremony; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Catherine (Kate), are due to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday. The couple will arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening at a ceremony in the city.

The couple, who were originally scheduled to spend their entire visit in Mumbai, will now conclude it with a meeting with Mr. Modi. Their schedule was changed on Sunday after Mr. Modi’s travel plans were confirmed, the Sunday Times reported. The Prime Minister is due to return from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Summit in the Philippines on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly, Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by the Prince in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crore) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.
India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s event.
When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest among 15,000 schools across 24 States.

“The future of the U.K.-India partnership will not be shaped by our governments alone, it will be shaped by our people and this visit is a wonderful opportunity to celebrate those deep personal connections between our countries,” said Ben Mellor, Acting British High Commissioner to India, according to PTI.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and the Princess’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

articles.title: West Bengal BJP president alleges conversions at missionary schools; draws flak
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches

West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chief Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 15, 2026) warned Christian missionary schools in the State over alleged religious conversions taking place at these institutions.

“If in Christian missionary schools there are anti-India activities on the grounds of religion and colour, we will not allow such schools to continue. In one school, an authority has kept the flag of Pakistan on the table... Another reputed school has asked one of its teachers not to attend the school wearing saffron saris,” Mr. Bhattacharya claimed at an event.

This is the first time a senior State BJP leader has made remarks about the community, even as Christian groups have protested against attacks on churches. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP), an umbrella forum of Christian organisations, urged Mr. Bhattacharya to publicly name the schools.

“If anyone has indeed engaged in such conduct, it is highly condemnable. However, making sweeping generalisations about Christian missionary schools in public without naming the institutions involved is irresponsible, condemnable and dangerous,” said BCP founding secretary Herod Mullick.

Earlier in the day, CM Suvendu Adhikari accused the previous Trinamool Congress government of considering only Muslims as a minority community, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains also qualify as religious minorities.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

articles.title: As diabetes spikes in Kashmir, the health lens turns to the fabled wazwan
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living has been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns persist largely unchanged, the doctor-authors of Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir say

The Kashmiri wazwan , an array of dishes adding up to 4,500-5,500 calories partaken during festivals and weddings, is one of the key cultural factors contributing to a spike in cases of diabetes in Kashmir, experts said.

Kashmir’s social life is organised around large, meat-centred feasts, most visibly the wazwan served at weddings or on Eid. Diabetes Simplified for Kashmir , a book released on World Diabetes Day (November 14), said the multi-course meal can run to over 30 mutton and chicken preparations, with the calorie intake “several times the average daily requirement”.

“Such exposure accumulates rather than occurs in isolation, and repeated post-prandial glucose and lipid excursions of this magnitude plausibly contribute to the region’s rising dysglycaemia burden,” the book, co-authored by endocrinologists Mohammad Hayat Bhat and Shahnawaz Mir, and cardiologist Nasir Shams, stated.
Degchis (traditional heavy-bottomed cooking pots) filled with wazwan dishes at a wedding feast in Srinagar. | Photo Credit: Reuters

J&K has witnessed a spike in the incidence of diabetes in the past three years. The Union Territory screened more than 2.15 million people for diabetes; 48,623 individuals have been diagnosed to have diabetes, according to data from the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. In 2025-2026, 2.84 million people were screened and 85,948 were found to have diabetes. “In the past three years, J&K added 2.18 lakh new patients to its diabetes burden,” the Ministry’s data suggested.
Apart from more universally seen factors, including poor physical activity and consumption of tobacco, the book identifies Kashmir’s unique lifestyle among the contributing factors.

“Kashmir’s daily plate remains rice-centric with rice typically supplying the bulk of meal volume and carbohydrate load. Large portions of rice translate directly into high postprandial glycaemic load,” it said.

“Type 2 diabetes prevalence in Kashmir has risen sharply within a single generation. A survey in 1999 found known diabetes in just 1.89% of adults, with 4.25% undiagnosed. Recent Indian Council of Medical Research-INDIA data show 7.8% prevalence,” the authors said, attributing the rising incidence of Type 2 diabetes to lifestyle in Kashmir.

The book noted that such a rapid shift cannot reflect genetic change. “It points instead to a compressed nutrition and lifestyle transition, as subsistence agriculture and labour-intensive living have been replaced by urbanisation and declining physical activity, while traditional dietary patterns — rice-centric meals, salt tea, preserved winter foods, and elaborate festive feasting — persist largely unchanged,” the experts said.

They also attributed the rise in cases of diabetes to Kashmir’s winters. “The glycaemic and fat load of the traditional meat and generous portion sizes do not act in isolation. Their convergence with a pronounced winter sedentary period appears to produce a compounding rather than merely additive metabolic burden across the Kashmiri annual cycle, in which periods of highest intake coincide with the lowest levels of expenditure,” they added.

articles.title: Punjab BJP forms manifesto, 'chargesheet' committees
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The members of this committee include Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Vijay Sampla, Shwet Malik, Maharani Preneet Kaur, Ravneet Singh Bittu, Dinesh Babbu, Sushil Rinku, Geja Ram, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Ashok Mittal, Sandeep Pathak, S.S. Channi, and Jagmeet Singh Brar
Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Sunday (November 15, 2026) constituted a State manifesto committee and a "chargesheet" committee ahead of the 2027 State Assembly elections.

Senior BJP leader Avinash Rai Khanna will head the party's manifesto committee, while other BJP leaders — Manpreet Singh Badal, Ashwani Sharma, Manoranjan Kalia, Som Parkash, Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi, Ashwani Sekhri, Satnam Singh Sandhu, Raghav Chadha, Rajinder Gupta, Harbhajan Singh, Parampal Kaur, and H.S. Phoolka will be its members, according to a party statement.
Former Punjab chief Sunil Jakhar has been appointed chairman of the "chargesheet" committee.

The members of this committee include Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Vijay Sampla, Shwet Malik, Maharani Preneet Kaur, Ravneet Singh Bittu, Dinesh Babbu, Sushil Rinku, Geja Ram, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Ashok Mittal, Sandeep Pathak, S.S. Channi, and Jagmeet Singh Brar.
By including senior leaders in the manifesto committee, the party has brought together their experience and representation from various fields for preparing its election manifesto, it said.
Similarly, senior leaders have also been included in the "chargesheet" committee and entrusted with a distinct responsibility, it said.

articles.title: In latest ‘encounter’, West Bengal police kill a man accused of shooting at a constable two days ago
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is the fifth instance of an accused killed in police firing in West Bengal, within six months of the BJP coming to power in the State; this was an “extrajudicial execution”, says civil society group

A man accused of opening fire at a police constable at Santiniketan in West Bengal 's Birbhum district on Friday (November 13, 2026) was killed in a gunfight with the law enforcers on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a senior officer said.
Ratan Sheikh was killed after he opened fire at a police team while trying to evade arrest at a brick kiln in Nanoor in the same district.
This was the fifth police encounter in West Bengal in six months since the BJP came to power in the State.

Sheikh, a history-sheeter who was absconding, allegedly shot at constable Biswajit Das, injuring him in the leg, during an arrest attempt at Laik Bazar in Santiniketan police station area on November 13.
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, while reacting to the development, asks reporters, "If someone opens fire at the police, should the police offer them sweets"

A man accused of opening fire at a police constable at Santiniketan in West Bengal 's Birbhum district on Friday (November 13, 2026) was killed in a gunfight with the law enforcers on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a senior officer said.

articles.title: Funds sought to clear traffic gridlocks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have been demanding steps to clear traffic bottlenecks on the stretch that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass, considering the immense potential the road holds to decongest the bypass. On widening Vennala Junction, Uma Thomas, MLA, says apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic

With plans afoot to widen the severely bottlenecked Vennala Junction under a ₹1 crore project, demand is rife to widen the two narrow and similarly choked trijunctions on either side of the junction and also Alinchuvadu Junction where traffic snarls are the norm.
Vehicles jostling for space at the congested Alinchuvadu Junction. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

Apart from motorists, residents’ and merchants’ bodies have over the years been demanding that the State government allot funds to clear traffic bottlenecks on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that runs parallel to the Palarivattom-Kundannur NH bypass stretch, considering the immense potential the road held to decongest the bypass.

Over the past few years, serpentine traffic snarls have been the norm at Vennala Junction and at the three other junctions on Alinchuvadu-Vennala-Eroor road that is increasingly being used by IT professionals and others who travel from the NH bypass towards Infopark, other places in Kakkanad, and Thripunithura, said Sabu Koroth, councillor representing Vennala (Division 38) in the Kochi Corporation.
The bottlenecked Vennala Junction. Traffic snarls have been the norm at the Junction for years. | Photo Credit: H. VIBHU

“A committee comprising people’s representatives and others was constituted following a stakeholder meeting that was held recently to collate suggestions from members of the public on decongesting Vennala Junction. The suggestions would be submitted to Thrikkakara MLA Uma Thomas and later on to the District Collector, based on which a master plan to decongest the region is set to be readied,” he said.

It is high time adequate funds were allotted to widen the three other extremely narrow junctions (Alinchuvadu, V-Guard Junction, and Sundarimukku) as well to ensure smooth and safe movement of vehicles and pedestrians in the corridor, Mr. Koroth said.

On the proposal to widen Vennala Junction, the MLA said that apart from widening the junction’s bell mouth, land might have to be acquired at approximately one metre width from either side of the junction to ensure smooth flow of traffic.
The bell mouth of the junctions north and south of Vennala too must be widened for commuters to make optimal use of the road corridor, suggested Rajesh Vennala, a social worker from the area.

This is crucial since traffic would increase manifold when MG Road-Pullepady-Thammanam-NH bypass road that is slated to be four-laned, is extended further eastward from Chakkaraparambu on the NH bypass to Seaport-Airport Road through largely puramboke lands, he said.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis

fullParagraphs: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February

Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.summary: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society
articles.keyPoints:
• This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society
• A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.
• One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.summary: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
articles.keyPoints:
• Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently
• If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.
• In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

fullParagraphs: The Indian Institute of Chemical Engineers – Hyderabad Regional Centre (IIChE-HRC) organised Dr. H. L. Roy memorial seminar on Saturday in the Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) on the theme - Innovations in Green Technologies & Sustainable Manufacturing: Shaping the Future of Chemical Engineering.
The seminar commemorated Dr. Hira Lal Roy, the founding father of chemical engineering education and research in India, who established IIChE in 1947.

The inaugural session commenced with a welcome address by M. Misra, chairman, IIChE-HRC, who highlighted the significance of the seminar theme and the role of chemical engineers in promoting sustainable industrial development.

Dr. Komal Kapoor, Chairman & Chief Executive, NFC, emphasised the importance of technological innovation, operational excellence and sustainable practices in the nuclear sector. He elaborated the role of chemical engineer from ore to core and importance in reprocessing.

M. Narayana Reddy, Managing Director (Technical), Virchow Laboratories Limited, highlighted the need for industry–academia collaboration, adoption of green technologies and development of sustainable manufacturing practices to address emerging industrial challenges.

The technical sessions featured six eminent speakers representing premier research, academic and industrial organisations, who included Dr. S. K. Satpati, OS & Head, UED, MG/BARC, DAE; Shri Darshan B. Sathe, Executive Director, Fuel Fabrication, INRP(O), NRB, BARC; Prof. Dr. Chandra Shekhar Sharma, Head, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Hyderabad; Dr. S. Sridhar, Chief Scientist & Chair (CE & PT), CSIR-IICT; Shri Mahimabrata Misra, General Manager, NFC; and Dr. Venkata Nori, Co-Founder & CEO, AltNxt Energy Pvt. Ltd.
The event witnessed the participation of 120 delegates.
The seminar reinforced the vital role of chemical engineers in advancing clean energy, resource efficiency, technological innovation and sustainable industrial development, informed a press release.

articles.title: AIADMK to protest seeking action against Deputy Speaker in Thuraiyur ‘assault’ incident
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Edappadi K. Palaniswami criticises Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue

The AIADMK has announced a protest on November 18, demanding action over an alleged incident in which M. Ravisankar, the TVK MLA for Thuraiyur and Deputy Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assaulted a social activist.

In a statement, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami alleged that Karthik Kumar, a social activist who went to meet Mr. Ravisankar to submit grievances, was subjected to a “brutal attack” and “verbal abuse”.

Mr. Palaniswami further claimed that after evidence of the assault surfaced, Mr. Ravisankar threatened the activist again and used a police officer to coerce the victim into posting on social media that the incident had never occurred. He remarked that this demonstrated how brazenly TVK legislators were engaging in hooliganism, which surpassed even what was depicted in films.

Criticising Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay for remaining silent on the issue, Mr. Palaniswami announced that the AIADMK would stage a condemnation protest at 10 a.m. on Wednesday (November 18 near the Anna Statue at the Thuraiyur bus stand, demanding strict action against Mr. Ravisankar.

articles.title: Exhibition, poster competitions held at CMC to mark World Diabetes Day
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As part of the screening initiative, blood glucose testing was conducted for more than 350 participants
An awareness exhibition and poster competitions were held at Christian Medical College (CMC) to commemorate World Diabetes Day 2026.
According to a press release, the event, which was organised by the Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, CMC, was centred around this year’s global theme - ‘Early Action on Diabetes.’

It was inaugurated by Vaibhav Londhe, associate director (Administration), CMC, and aims to increase awareness on diabetes prevention, early diagnosis, and holistic management, while emphasizing the importance of timely screening education and care.

As part of the screening initiative, blood glucose testing was conducted for more than 350 participants, who also benefited from foot and eye examinations. Awareness sessions were creatively delivered through puppet shows, posters, and interactive games, making learning both engaging and impactful, the release said.

articles.title: NCP merger talks ended with death of Ajit Pawar, says Supriya Sule
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Date was set for merger of two NCP factions, but talks ended the day the former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister died, says his cousin Supriya Sule

Putting a “full stop” on the discussion of a potential merger between the two Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) factions, NCP(Sharad Pawar) MP Supriya Sule said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the talks ended with the death of her cousin Ajit Pawar , the former national president of the rival faction.

“The merger talks were on till my brother was alive and the date was set. The day he died, the talks were given a full stop. Our spokesperson never made statements on it or gave counters to rival faction,” Ms. Sule told the media.
Ajit Pawar, the former Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, died in an aircraft accident on January 28 at Baramati airport in Pune.

The speculation of a possible reunion between the rival factions have been intensifying over the last few days amid several high-profile meetings, including between senior NCP working president Praful Patel and NCP(SP) supremo Sharad Pawar. Meanwhile, current Deputy Chief Minister and NCP national president Sunetra Pawar met Chief Minister and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday.

NCP MP Sunil Tatkare dismissed any political intention behind Mr. Patel’s meeting with Mr. Sharad Pawar and called it a personal visit. The buzz of merger had intensified after senior NCP leaders met Union Home Minister Amit Shah and it gained further momentum ahead of Mr. Shah’s scheduled visit to Pune on Sunday (November 15).

Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut advised NCP(SP) not to get swept away in the merger game for ministerial posts, saying “there may be a handful of people in Sharad Pawar’s party desperate for ministerial posts but it is not right for Sharad Pawar to destroy the principles he has upheld throughout his life for their sake.”

The leader of the NCP(SP)’s Opposition ally also highlighted that it does not suit the faction to discuss matters with a group that “licks the BJP’s boots” and create an “atmosphere of confusion” in Maharashtra.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi promises social security, insurance cover for gig workers in Telangana
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security

Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy along with Gig Workers launches the Telangana Gig Workers Social Security and Welfare Scheme at Hitech City, Hyderabad on Saturday, as part of the Bharat Summit. | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi announced a series of social security measures for gig workers in Telangana, including accident insurance of ₹5 lakh, health insurance of ₹10 lakh, dedicated Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones and a mechanism to ensure that 1% of every transaction is credited towards their social security.

Addressing gig workers, Mr. Gandhi said the Congress government in Telangana was fulfilling its promise to protect workers engaged in the platform-based economy and ensure that they received their fair share of the benefits generated by their labour.

Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy riding pillion on two-wheelers while participating in a rally from Indira Gandhi statue to Jayabheri Grounds, in Hyderabad on Saturday (November 14). | Photo Credit: NAGARA GOPAL

Describing the 21st century as the age of data, Mr. Gandhi pointed out that while companies such as Google, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Uber operated on data, gig workers had so far been denied access to information about their own work.

Under the proposed legislation, workers would be able to access complete details of their transactions, deliveries, working hours, and payments through their mobile phones. “The data belongs to you, the labour is yours, but you were not even allowed to see your own data,” he said.

He said the government would also establish dedicated, Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones in Hyderabad and other cities to enable delivery personnel and other gig workers to park their vehicles, rest and relax during working hours.

Announcing insurance benefits, Mr. Gandhi said every gig worker would receive ₹5 lakh in accident insurance and ₹10 lakh in health insurance. A social security contribution mechanism under which 1% of every transaction, including deliveries and cab rides, would be contributed towards the workers’ future security.
The amount would be collected from companies and routed through the Gig Workers’ Board before being transferred directly to the workers’ bank accounts, he said.

Drawing a political distinction between the Congress and the BJP-RSS, Mr. Gandhi alleged that the latter wanted to turn gig workers into bonded labourers while allowing large corporate houses and platform companies to reap the benefits. In contrast, the Congress believed that workers were the foundation of the country’s economy and should be treated as partners.

articles.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements.

Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony and unveiling of the campus master plan on Saturday, Mr. Reddy said the government was committed to developing the institution into a world-class university that would contribute to public health education, research and healthcare in India and internationally.

He further added that the proposed university was not merely another educational institution but a project of global significance. Expressing confidence in its potential, he said he hoped that in the coming years, people would discuss the PHFI university alongside established institutions such as Harvard and Oxford.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub. He said individuals who had established successful institutions had helped create a distinct identity for the city and that the PHFI university would add to this legacy.
PHFI Chairman Rajat Gupta said the university aspired to achieve excellence through world-class faculty, students, international collaborations and infrastructure.

PHFI IPHS Chancellor Dr. K. Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad. Dr. Reddy said the foundation’s work involved advancing multidisciplinary education and research through multi-sectoral implementation and multi-stakeholder engagement. The objective was to improve life expectancy, strengthen health systems, align policies across sectors with population health goals and encourage active community engagement.

Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities. He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

Vice-Chancellor M. Vishnu Vardhana Rao outlined the university’s academic journey and expansion plans. The Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad was established in 2008 under the aegis of PHFI, with the objective of advancing public health through education, research and community engagement. The institution received recognition as a deemed-to-be university from the University Grants Commission in 2025, with Hyderabad as its main campus and Bengaluru as another campus, he said.

With the proposed campus and modern infrastructure, the institution plans to expand its academic offerings to at least six postgraduate programmes, two undergraduate programmes, PhD programmes and institute-level Master of Public Health programmes. It aims to build an academic community of approximately 2,500 students and research scholars over the next five years.

Dr. Rao said the university’s research priorities would include infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, One Health, mental health and disability. Digital health, artificial intelligence and data science would serve as cross-cutting areas across its research activities, he added.

articles.title: TGPCB recommends closures, forfeitures over dusty construction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) has received several complaints regarding air pollution caused by dust emissions from construction projects in the Tellapur and Kollur areas of Sangareddy district. After receiving several complaints of air pollution due to construction, the Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) constituted Rolling Task Force Teams to these projects and assess compliance with environmental regulations and implementation of air pollution control measures.

The team embarked on inspections and observed dust emissions from construction activity was aggravating air pollution. Several violations of environmental norms were also identified, the TGPCB stated.

The Committee reviewed the environmental compliance of as many as 16 construction projects. After examining the severity of the violations, committee recommended the issuing of closure orders against projects where serious violations were identified, along with the forfeiture of bank guarantees. The committee also recommended forfeiture of bank guarantees in respect of projects where minor violations were observed. A period of 10 days was recommended for the concerned projects to rectify the violations.

Three construction projects began construction activity without obtaining Consent for Establishment (CFE) from the Pollution Control Board, the TGPCB stated. The committee recommended the issuance of closure orders against these projects, it added. Two others were continuing construction activities in violation of the Orders for Suspension of Operations previously issued by the TGPCB, without obtaining permission from the Board for revocation of the suspension orders.

A Ready Mix Concrete plant operating in association with another construction project was found to be functioning without obtaining Consent for Operation (CFO) from the TGPCB. The plant was also found to be lacking adequate air pollution control measures, thereby contributing to air pollution in the surrounding areas. The Task Force Committee recommended closure of the operations of this RMC plant as well.

articles.title: Six-month traffic disruption ahead as Ranigunj railway underpass work to begin in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The existing 13-metre carriageway will be widened to 22 metres, allowing four-way traffic movement, with an additional three metres of road space sought at Karbala Maidan to facilitate one-way movement during diversions.

For motorists navigating the Ranigunj rail underpass during peak hours, the familiar sight is a long queue of vehicles inching towards the narrow passage from Tank Bund, with buses, trucks, cars and two-wheelers jostling for space. What should be a short passage into a frustrating bottleneck. The proposed widening promises relief, but commuters will have to negotiate six months of traffic diversions before the work is completed.

Work on widening the Ranigunj Road Under Bridge (RuB) is expected to begin within a week. The existing carriageway, which is around 13 metres wide and currently accommodates two-way traffic, will be expanded to 22 metres to facilitate four-way movement. Officials expect the additional width to ease congestion and improve traffic flow along the busy stretch.

Traffic will be diverted through alternative routes. Under the proposed plan, vehicles travelling from MG Road towards Paradise and Ranigunj will be asked to take a left towards Distillery Road, pass through another road underbridge and proceed towards Karbala before joining MG Road.

Buses and trucks will be diverted from Old Ambedkar towards Liberty, Kavadiguda and Musheerabad, while smaller vehicles will be routed through Karbala and Ranigunj. To facilitate smoother movement at Karbala, the concerned agency has been asked to provide an additional three metres of road space to enable one-way traffic.

Officials said that if congestion builds up near Karbala Maidan, a portion of the traffic will be diverted through Minister Road and Rasoolpura. Flexi boards and signboards have been put up along the stretch to alert motorists about the upcoming work and diversions.

Hyderabad, Telangana, 14/11/2026: A view of Ranigunj railway underpass near James Street railway station as part of the six-month traffic disruption ahead as underpass work to begin, in Secunderabad on Saturday, November 14, 2026. Photo: RAMAKRISHNA G/The Hindu | Photo Credit: RAMAKRISHNA G

A. Chandra Shekar, who works at the Nampally court, commutes every day from Bolarum to reach work by 9 a.m., travelling through the stretch during the morning rush hour. He said the diversions would mean a longer commute for the next six months, but felt the eventual improvement would justify the inconvenience. “Although it will be a struggle to make the extra ride to dodge the stretch for six months, I speak for everyone when I say that this will bring much relief to a lot of commuters,” he said.

For Kalpana C, the congestion is not restricted to peak hours. She travels along Hussain Sagar Road from Himayatnagar towards her home in Rasoolpura and said the stretch frequently gets choked. “I take the Hussain Sagar Road to come home in Rasoolpura from Himayatnagar and it chokes up at any given time. Check the maps and it will be red constantly, especially the road towards Paradise from Tank Bund,” she said.

An official traffic advisory detailing the vehicle-wise diversion routes and restrictions will be issued by the Hyderabad Traffic Police before construction begins. Commuters will be advised to follow the notified routes and plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Traffic diversions for steel flyover construction in Banjara Hills
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Traffic restrictions and diversions will be implemented on stretches between Srinagar Colony T-Junction and NTR Bhavan on Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, in view of the ongoing construction of a steel flyover between Jubilee Hills Check Post and NFCL under the H-CITI project.

According to the traffic advisory issued on Saturday, vehicles travelling from Srinagar Colony towards SNT Junction near the TV9 office and Road No. 2, Banjara Hills, will not be allowed to take a right turn at SNT Junction. Commuters will have to take a left turn and make a U-turn at NFCL to reach Road No. 2.

Vehicles coming from Begumpet towards SNT, Sagar Society, KBR Park entrance, Jubilee Hills Check Post, Road Nos. 36 and 45, and the Durgam Cheruvu Cable Bridge will have to take the Panjagutta Flyover ‘Y’ Junction towards Taj Krishna and Road No. 1, Banjara Hills. They should then take a right turn at the 1/10 Banjara Hills Junction towards Zaheranagar, Basavatarakam Cancer Hospital and Agarasen Island to reach their destinations.

Commuters travelling from Srinagar Colony towards NTR Bhavan and the Cable Bridge have been advised to proceed through Indiranagar Gadda, Venkatagiri and Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 10 and 36 towards Madhapur.

Vehicles coming from NFCL towards NTR Bhavan, Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 45 and 36, and Madhapur should take a right turn at Sagar Society ‘T’ Junction and proceed through Indiranagar Gadda, Srinagar Colony Main Road, Road No. 5, Venkatagiri Junction and Jubilee Hills Road Nos. 10 and 36.

The traffic police have advised commuters to avoid peak-hour travel between 8.30 a.m. and 11 a.m. and 5 p.m. and 9 p.m., wherever possible. They have also asked motorists to follow traffic police instructions and road signage, use navigation applications for updates, and prefer public transport and carpooling.
Commuters can contact the traffic helpline on 9010203626 for travel assistance. Traffic updates will also be available on the Hyderabad Traffic Police social media platforms.

articles.title: Eight varieties of pharmaceutical ingredients worth ₹3.54 lakh seized in TG SAFE raid at Ameenpur firm
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The drugs wing of the Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) seized illegally stocked Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) worth ₹3.54 lakh during a raid at a private company in Sultanpur village of Ameenpur mandal in Sangareddy district.

The raid was conducted at Neocell Biotechnologies Private Limited, located at the Medical Devices Park in Sultanpur, on Friday, following credible information about the illegal stocking of pharmaceutical ingredients for sale without a valid drug licence.

According to TG SAFE, officials found eight varieties of APIs illegally stocked at the premises and seized drug stocks worth ₹3.54 lakh. Further investigation is under way, and action will be initiated against those responsible in accordance with the law, TG SAFE said.

They further added that stocking APIs for sale without a valid drug licence is punishable under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, with imprisonment of up to five years. TG SAFE’s Drugs Wing is responsible for issuing licences for the stocking and sale of APIs under the Act.

articles.title: Four arrested for illegal sand extraction in Madgul

fullParagraphs: Four persons were arrested for allegedly extracting sand illegally from Madgul lake and transporting it without authorisation during the early hours of November 11.

The accused were identified as Kasani Mallesh, Gaddam Jangaiah, M. Jagadeesh and Katla Raju. According to Madgul police, they excavated soil from the lake, filtered it to extract sand and transported it illegally at around 3 a.m.

Police arrested the four as part of the investigation and produced them before a magistrate at Amangal. The court remanded them to judicial custody for 15 days, following which they were shifted to Chanchalguda Central Prison.
The Future City police warned that strict legal action would be taken against those involved in illegal sand extraction, transportation and other unlawful activities.

The bilateral talk was aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation and further deepening navy-to-navy engagements between the two countries.
On arrival, he paid homage to fallen soldiers by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial. Thereafter, he was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour at the South Block lawns.
He also interacted with other senior officials to explore avenues for enhancing bilateral cooperation. India and Belgium share longstanding maritime linkages.

The visit marks an important milestone in bilateral navy-to-navy relations and is expected to provide impetus to maritime cooperation through strengthening existing engagements and exploration of new avenues for collaboration, the official said.

articles.title: In Jharkhand, even jails are not safe: Babulal Marandi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Launching a sharp attack on Sorens’ government, Mr. Marandi said law and order in Jharkhand has collapsed and it raises serious questions on the functioning of the government
The Leader of the Opposition in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 14, 2026), cornered the State Government over a series of criminal incidents.

He cited the incidents of including the sexual assault of a youth in Hotwar Jail, the alleged rape of a minor girl by a Congress MLA from Simdega, and the alleged rape of a woman who had gone to the Gamharia police station seeking justice.

Fifteen police officers were suspended in connection with the alleged rape of a 20-year-old woman on the premises of the Gamharia police station in Jharkhand, Saraikela-Kharsawan district, on November 1, 2026.
Launching a sharp attack on Sorens’ government, Mr. Marandi said law and order in Jharkhand has collapsed and it raises serious questions on the functioning of the government.
Addressing a press conference at the state Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) office in Ranchi, Mr. Marandi said that such incidents are continuously coming to light, and they are deeply disturbing.

“Today, in Jharkhand, neither jails nor police stations nor the residences of legislators are safe. What has happened to Jharkhand? How have conditions in the state deteriorated to such an extent that ordinary citizens no longer feel safe anywhere?” Mr. Marandi said.
Expressing concern over the incident at Hotwar Jail, Mr. Marandi asserted that while a jail is considered the most secure place, even there, prisoners are not safe.
A man has recently filed a police complaint against 19 people, including Birsa Munda Central Jail officials, alleging severe abuse of his 20-year-old son inside the jail.
The father had accused jail inmates and staff of sexual assault of his son and forced him to consume narcotics while he stayed there as an undertrial prisoner.

“A 20-year-old youth was allegedly subjected to gang sexual assault. This incident is truly chilling. When the victim filed a written complaint, it was torn, and he was not even provided with proper medical treatment,” Mr. Marandi said.

Launching a sharp attack on Sorens’ government, Mr. Marandi said law and order in Jharkhand has collapsed and it raises serious questions on the functioning of the government

The Leader of the Opposition in the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly Babulal Marandi on Saturday (November 14, 2026), cornered the State Government over a series of criminal incidents.

He cited the incidents of including the sexual assault of a youth in Hotwar Jail, the alleged rape of a minor girl by a Congress MLA from Simdega, and the alleged rape of a woman who had gone to the Gamharia police station seeking justice.

Fifteen police officers were suspended in connection with the alleged rape of a 20-year-old woman on the premises of the Gamharia police station in Jharkhand, Saraikela-Kharsawan district, on November 1, 2026.

Launching a sharp attack on Sorens’ government, Mr. Marandi said law and order in Jharkhand has collapsed and it raises serious questions on the functioning of the government.

Addressing a press conference at the state Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) office in Ranchi, Mr. Marandi said that such incidents are continuously coming to light, and they are deeply disturbing.

“Today, in Jharkhand, neither jails nor police stations nor the residences of legislators are safe. What has happened to Jharkhand? How have conditions in the state deteriorated to such an extent that ordinary citizens no longer feel safe anywhere?” Mr. Marandi said.

Expressing concern over the incident at Hotwar Jail, Mr. Marandi asserted that while a jail is considered the most secure place, even there, prisoners are not safe.

A man has recently filed a police complaint against 19 people, including Birsa Munda Central Jail officials, alleging severe abuse of his 20-year-old son inside the jail.

The father had accused jail inmates and staff of sexual assault of his son and forced him to consume narcotics while he stayed there as an undertrial prisoner.

“A 20-year-old youth was allegedly subjected to gang sexual assault. This incident is truly chilling. When the victim filed a written complaint, it was torn, and he was not even provided with proper medical treatment,” Mr. Marandi said.

articles.title: Villagers in 25 districts cast votes for panchayat elections’ final phase in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The final phase polls across 25 districts for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti faced EVM glitches, boycotts, and a 72% turnout

Villagers in 25 districts of Rajasthan cast their votes for the fourth and final phase of polling on Saturday to elect the Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti members at a total of 2,524 seats. An estimated 72% turnout of voters at 11,905 polling stations was recorded by the end of the day.

The polling for first, second and third phases of Panchayati Raj elections was held on October 22, October 28 and November 3, respectively. Counting of votes for Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections across all four phases will be held on November 20, followed by elections for Zila Pramukhs and Panchayat Samiti Pradhans.

There were delays in polling at several places due to glitches in electronic voting machines (EVMs), while the voters at some villages in Baran and Jaisalmer districts boycotted the polling to press for their demands.

The villagers at Mundakya and Mundki in Baran boycotted the voting in protest against an irrigation project adversely affecting their lands. They have been demanding fair compensation for land acquisition for the project. The villagers at Bhojraj Ki Dhani in Jaisalmer did not cast their votes in protest against alleged anomalies in the reservation for Other Backward Classes.

Police took two persons into custody at a polling station in Sikar district’s Hapas village when they created a commotion while insisting on carrying their mobile phones inside the booth. The situation escalated when they began arguing with the polling officials and the policemen, leading to their detention on charges of disturbing peace.

The highest polling at 77% was reported at Baseri in Dholpur district. A total of 8,843 candidates are contesting 2,524 seats in the fourth phase, including 382 Zila Parishad wards and 2,142 Panchayat Samiti wards. There are 1,322 contestants for Zila Parishad seats and 7,521 for Panchayat Samiti wards.

Bharatiya Janata Party leader and former Minister Rajendra Rathore’s son Parakram Singh and daughter-in-law, Kanika, are among the prominent candidates contesting for Zila Parishad seats from Churu district.

The final phase of polling covered Balotra, Baran, Banswara, Beawar, Bharatpur, Bikaner, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Churu, Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Dholpur, Hanumangarh, Jalore, Jaipur, Jhunjhunu, Jaisalmer, Karauli, Khairthal-Tijara, Pratapgarh, Sawai Madhopur, Salumber, Sikar, Sriganganagar and Tonk districts.

articles.title: Mumbai police announce traffic diversion ahead of Britain’s Prince William visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ceremony is hosted in Mumbai from November 16 to 18 for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize

Mumbai Police on Saturday (November 14, 2026) have announced traffic diversions, road closures and parking restrictions across parts of south Mumbai from November 16 to 19 in view of a VVIP visit to the city. The restrictions come ahead of Britain’s Prince William’s visit to Mumbai for the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony.
The ceremony is hosted in Mumbai from November 16 to 18 for the sixth annual Earthshot Prize.

The notification issued by Hemrajsingh Rajput, Deputy Commissioner of Police (South), Traffic, Mumbai, includes changes to traffic movement around Hutatma Rajguru Chowk, Shaheed Bhagatsingh Marg, Ballard Pier and several roads in the NCPA area.

The pay and park are suspended on Vinay K. Shah Marg road and Dorabji Tata Road for 24 hours, and on November 16, the parking is suspended from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. on Moraji Road, J. N. Media Marg, and Walchand Hirachand Marg.

The U-turn from Free Press Road’s northbound carriageway at Hutatma Rajguru Chowk towards the southbound carriageway will be permitted during this period and the right turn from Madam Cama Road towards Free press road will remain open.

The restrictions were also made on the movement of vehicles towards the Ballard Pier alighting point on November 16. From 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., the route from Shahid Bhagat Singh Marg to Avtarsingh Bedi Chowk and then right towards Walchand Hirachand Marg will remain open only to vehicles carrying VVIPs.

articles.title: Bomb rips through Damascus suburb; killing 2, including child

fullParagraphs: The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said

An explosive device placed inside a car in a suburb of Syria’s capital exploded on Saturday evening (November 15, 2026), killing two people and wounding at least one, state TV and the Interior Ministry said.

The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said. It said two people were killed and two were wounded, without giving further details.
The Interior Ministry said the dead included a child, adding that one person was wounded. It said security forces cordoned off the area and started an investigation.

Several explosions have taken place in Damascus and its suburbs in recent months as the country’s security remains fragile nearly two years after five decades of Assad family rule ended in December 2024. Militants stormed the capital and removed then-President Bashar Assad from power.

Jaramana is home to a large community of the Druze religious minority. The suburb has faced tensions between some members of the community and Sunni Muslim Syrians supportive of the country’s current Islamist-led government.

articles.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months
SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday (November 14, 2026), caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.
Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.
“Can you believe it?” shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.

NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.

The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-metre) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.

Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps.
It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.
SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.

🎯 Exam Relevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy

SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months

SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday (November 14, 2026), caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.

Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.

“Can you believe it?” shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.

NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.

The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-metre) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.

Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometres) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps.

It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.

SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.
