articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Disruption to Microsoft’s cloud-based email service affects business operations and airline customer support in India; public services in several countries also report problems

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. articles.title: MP adds 8.19 lakh voters since final SIR roll, electorate rises to 5.48 crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons

Madhya Pradesh has recorded an addition of 8.19 lakh voters in the draft electoral roll published under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, taking the state's total electorate to nearly 5.48 crore, two years ahead of the next assembly elections, officials said.

Compared with the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in February this year, the latest draft, released on Thursday (November 12, 2026), shows an addition of 4,38,361 women, 3,80,169 men and 33 transgender voters, according to Election Commission (EC) figures.
With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons.
The State had 5,39,81,065 voters, including 2,79,04,975 males, 2,60,75,186 females and 904 transgender persons, when the SIR list was published in February.
Age-wise data shows that the 30-39 age bracket accounts for the highest number of voters at 1,40,50,865, followed by the 20-29 age group at 1,29,48,107.
The EC has invited claims and objections till December 11, following which the final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
ALSO WATCH Madhya Pradesh: Over 30 tribal children die in Balaghat, many hospitalised

The increase in the number of voters assumes significance as the SIR had triggered a political row, with the Congress alleging the removal of eligible voters and the ruling BJP defending the exercise, maintaining it was undertaken to purge the names of deceased, shifted, absent and duplicate voters.
Madhya Pradesh is scheduled to go to the polls towards the end of 2028. The state's population is projected to reach 9.05 crore, compared with 7.26 crore recorded in the 2011 Census.

Madhya Pradesh has 230 assembly seats, of which 47 are reserved for Scheduled Tribes and 35 for Scheduled Castes, and 29 Lok Sabha constituencies, including six reserved for Scheduled Tribes and four for Scheduled Castes.

articles.title: Rubio assails international court in speech to conservative legal group
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S., Mr. Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio attacked the International Criminal Court in a speech ​to a conservative legal group on Friday (November 13, 2026), arguing for a muscular foreign ⁠policy and against international law restraining U.S. actions.

Mr. Rubio’s speech to the Federalist Society in Washington, his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections on November 3 , heightens speculation over whether he ‌will leave his roles as national security adviser and top U.S. diplomat to run for president in 2028.

Mr. Rubio, who has at times sought to ‌provide an intellectual justification for President Donald Trump’s “America First” foreign policy, has firmly denied reports ‌he ⁠will soon embark on a presidential campaign, but the Federalist Society is ⁠an occasional stop for Republican hopefuls.

He has dismissed criticisms that the Trump administration has broken international law by such actions as seizing Venezuelan then-President Nicolas Maduro and striking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that it says ​were carrying drugs.

In his speech, Mr. Rubio said ‌the goal of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran was to prevent Tehran from ever developing a nuclear weapon, which he said was particularly urgent because the Islamic Republic’s “radical Shia clerics” had an “expansionist mentality.”

He contrasted this with the government of North Korea’s Kim Jong ‌Un, whom Mr. Trump has met three times. “I’m not excusing the terrible things that ​have happened there,” Rubio said of North Korea. “I’m just saying he [Kim] is not expansionist. He’s not trying to invade Japan or, you know, China ⁠or whatever.”

The U.S., Mr. Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats,” repeating his assertion that the court would try to prosecute US officials or ‌service members that he used to justify sanctions against the ICC announced last month.

“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order,” Mr. Rubio said.

The Trump administration has long been hostile to the Netherlands-based court, founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and has previously imposed sanctions on ‌its prosecutors and judges. The ICC has received strong backing from most member states, which include all EU ​countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkey.

Washington has denounced the court over arrest warrants issued for Israeli ⁠officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and an investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which ⁠the ICC says is “deprioritized.”

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which continued late into Friday, affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.
Microsoft outage disrupts global services, hitting Indian businesses, airlines, public sectors, with recovery underway and security advisories issued.

articles.title: Indian envoy slams USCIRF over Sharjeel Imam remarks, says panel has 'no locus standi'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In a strongly worded post on X, Vinay Kwatra rejected the commission’s assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India’s commitment to religious freedom and equal rights

India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) slammed the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) over its remarks on jailed activist Sharjeel Imam, asserting that the commission had "no locus standi" to pass judgment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.

In a strongly worded post on X , Mr. Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights. "USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Mr. Kwatra said.

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.

"India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others," he added.

The ambassador's remarks came after the USCIRF shared Imam's profile on X , describing him as "a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.” The commission's post characterised Mr. Imam's detention as being linked to his advocacy for religious freedom, a description that drew a sharp response from the Indian envoy.

Sharjeel Imam, a former student activist, was arrested in January 2020 in connection with protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), which took place in December 2019 and January 2020. Authorities accused him of delivering speeches that allegedly incited communal violence. In August 2020, he was charged in connection with FIR 59/2020, relating to the larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The charges invoked provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), including those relating to rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts. The case is being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell.

Separately, on October 10, a Delhi Court declined to entertain a Delhi Police plea seeking cancellation of Mr. Imam's seven-day interim bail, despite observing that he had apparently violated a condition restricting his interaction with the media. Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai of the Karkardooma Courts examined video footage submitted by the prosecution, which allegedly showed Imam present in a room where a media person was interviewing his brother. The prosecution contended that Mr. Imam had breached the bail conditions by coming into contact with a media person. However, his counsel denied the allegations, arguing that the footage did not establish any direct interaction between Imam and the journalist.

Imam had been granted interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to attend his cousin's wedding functions. The relief was subject to conditions prohibiting him from using social media, interacting with media persons and meeting individuals other than family members, relatives and friends. Taking note of the defence's submission that Mr. Imam had boarded a flight to Delhi and would surrender before jail authorities that evening, the Court declined to cancel his interim bail and disposed of the police application.

Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Huang resigned as ‌Nvidia CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry’s heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.

fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) on a mission the company hopes will ‌be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, ​a key test of Elon Musk’s effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship’s uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter ⁠the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and “chopstick”-arm technology to recover Starship’s lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within ‌minutes of the launch. But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface.
The booster for SpaceX's mega rocket Starship explodes after a catch attempt was aborted during a test flight from Starbase, Texas. | Photo Credit: AP

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship’s upper stage back to home base at the ‌end ⁠of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

Bringing the top portion ⁠of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its ​launch pad from SpaceX’s South Texas Starbase complex along the ‌Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship’s 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX’s satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take ‌less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk’s space and AI business ​views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which continued late into Friday, affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.
Microsoft outage disrupts global services, hitting Indian businesses, airlines, public sectors, with recovery underway and security advisories issued.

Microsoft said on Saturday that services across Teams, Outlook, Copilot and other applications had fully recovered, bringing an end to a massive global outage that disrupted online communication for businesses and government agencies for more than 24 hours.

During the disruption, Downdetector recorded a peak of nearly 200,000 user reports of issues across Microsoft services shortly after 1 pm New York time. While fresh reports of problems involving Outlook and Copilot subsequently declined, this did not initially indicate that services had been fully restored.
Microsoft says services are seeing widespread recovery after a major outage caused by a network capacity upgrade issue.

US media reports say DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin ruled out any connection between Microsoft’s disruption and the FAA outage that triggered a nationwide ground stop on Friday (November 13). Mullin also dismissed the possibility of a cyberattack, confirming that the ground stop had been lifted. He said authorities were working with airports to ensure passenger safety and access to essential medication.

US media reports say Microsoft has identified the cause of one of its largest outages to date. Experts told NBC News that the disruption highlights the growing complexity of large-scale computing networks and the risks associated with their expanding infrastructure.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.
The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

articles.title: Kurumba: a language and community fighting for visibility
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kurumbas of Keralam are an Adivasi community with a population of only 2,719 as of 2024, who speak Kurumba, an oral language without a script; with the Census classifying languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers as ‘others’, the future of the language appears bleak

The Kurumbas of Keralam are an Adivasi community who reside in the hilly forest regions of Attappady in Palakkad district. The community has been classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India. They are one of the five PVTGs in Keralam. As the Census exercise is under way, one of the most significant identifiers of the community is faced with a troubling question.

The community members speak Kurumba, an oral language with no script. This language is widely spoken by the people, even today, and is the primary language of communication among the Kurumba people. However, most outsiders do not use the language and therefore the community members are forced to either learn Malayalam or other languages in order to converse with others.

articles.title: No locus standi: Indian envoy hits back at USCIRF for remarks on Sharjeel Imam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X, describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”

Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra has asked an American advisory body to introspect on its own prejudices and stop lecturing others, after the bipartisan agency flagged arrests in India allegedly on religious grounds.

Mr. Kwatra’s sharp retort on Friday (November 13, 2026) came after the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X , describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”.

Former Jawaharlal Nehru University scholar Imam has been booked under UAPA (Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act) on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.
The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.
“USCIRF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens,” Kwatra said
“Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths,” he said.

He said India flourishes, defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. “Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others,” Mr. Kwatra said.
India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.
Established by the U.S. government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the U.S. State Department.

U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X, describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”

Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra has asked an American advisory body to introspect on its own prejudices and stop lecturing others, after the bipartisan agency flagged arrests in India allegedly on religious grounds.

Mr. Kwatra’s sharp retort on Friday (November 13, 2026) came after the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) shared Sharjeel Imam’s profile on X , describing him as “a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy”.

Former Jawaharlal Nehru University scholar Imam has been booked under UAPA (Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act) on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.

The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.

“USCIRF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens,” Kwatra said

“Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths,” he said.

He said India flourishes, defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. “Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others,” Mr. Kwatra said.

India describes USCIRF as a biased organisation that lacks credibility.

articles.title: Police fully empowered to curb drugs and substance abuse in the city: Kerala High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court clarified that the directions issued by the Single Bench would not stand in the way of the police maintaining “requisite vigil and attention” to all activities about drug and substance abuse
The Kerala High Court has observed that the police were fully empowered to enforce every measure to rid the State of drugs and substance abuse.

A division bench comprising Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji was considering an appeal filed by the government against a single-bench order setting aside the Kochi city police’s notices imposing restrictions on DJ parties and other events at star hotels, issued to Radisson Blu, a five-star hotel in the city.

The court clarified that the directions issued by the Single Bench would not stand in the way of the police maintaining “requisite vigil and attention” to all activities about drug and substance abuse.
“Prohibition may not always be the best way forward, but rather strict regulation”, the court stated.
Emphasising the role of police in keeping peace in society, the court stated that they should be seen as partners in everyday life, not enemies.

Additional Advocate General Muhammed Shah informed the court that the instructions in the notices issued by the Police were not to restrict the operation of bars until 3 a.m., only against “uncontrolled parties” where drugs and other substances are allegedly used, even openly.

Lawyer Anand Kalyanakrishnan, representing Radisson Blu, informed the court that the hotel was fully responsible for the parties and that they ensure that every customer was carefully screened and scrutinised for carrying drugs or other substances. The matter would be considered for detailed hearing on November 16.

articles.title: Mahadev betting app case: CBI searches in 6 States lead to recovery of digital devices, key documents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CBI has conducted searches at 33 locations across six States in connection with its investigation into the Mahadev online betting app case , recovering digital devices, mobile phones and documents indicating the use of mule bank accounts and hawala channels, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
The agency said it conducted searches based on disclosures from Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the platform's principal promoters, following his extradition from Oman.
The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises in Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal and Raipur, among others, linked to the betting platform's panel operators, they said.
The CBI spokesperson said live betting and gambling panels were found operating at several locations and subsequently dismantled.
The betting app promoter, Chandrakar, was extradited from Oman and arrested by the CBI on November 1.
A special court in Raipur had granted the agency eight days of police custody for his interrogation. He was later sent to judicial custody after the CBI completed its initial questioning.

"His interrogation revealed the details about the working of the platform and its network of panel operators in India," the CBI spokesperson said, adding that he was also confronted with documentary and digital evidence collected during the investigation.

"Investigation conducted so far has revealed that the platform is run from abroad through a Head Office and operates in India through a large network of panel operators," CBI Spokesperson Beena Yadav said in a statement.

She said these operators handle customer IDs, collect betting money in the bank accounts exclusively opened or hired in the names of other persons, and send the profits abroad through hawala channels.
The CBI has registered two FIRs in ₹6000-crore betting scam after the investigations were transferred to the central agency by the Chhattisgarh government.

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC in China: officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on November 19, 2026, on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers.

While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and they will be heavier in symbolism than substance.

Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday (November 13, 2026) by the White House. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.

Mr. Trump has warmly embraced Mr. Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Mr. Trump has sought to build his relationship with Mr. Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly five-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.

The U.S. President has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the U.S. war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Mr. Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China.

But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

By agreeing to host the meeting, Mr. Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige. “I would be shocked if there were a joint statement that came out of this meeting that said anything about denuclearisation,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.

articles.title: Samsung announces Google co-developed pricing and sale details of its smart glasses
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Equipped with a high-definition camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them

Samsung has officially unveiled its new lineup of intelligent eyewear , bringing hands-free artificial intelligence into everyday fashion. Developed in partnership with Google, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, the smart glasses integrate Google’s Gemini AI directly into stylish frames built for daily wear.

Set to launch on December 10, 2026, in the U.S. and South Korea, with pre-orders starting today, the collection features 30 distinct frame styles. Weighing around 41 grams, the frames combine Warby Parker’s classic look with Gentle Monster’s bold design aesthetics.

The smart glasses run on Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 platform. Equipped with a 12 MP HD camera, open-ear speakers, and directional microphones, the eyewear helps users interact naturally with the world around them. Wearers can ask Gemini to identify objects and landmarks, translate menus instantly or follow step-by-step navigation via Google Maps.

For workplace efficiency, the glasses can capture meeting whiteboards, generate key summaries and automatically sync them into Samsung Notes. The system also organises, summarises, and reads aloud incoming notifications.

To address privacy concerns, the eyewear design includes visible recording lights and audio chimes whenever the camera captures images or video. Additionally, the software claims to automatically blur bystanders’ faces during visual queries, while open-ear speakers are tuned to limit sound leakage.
The eyewear claims up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge, extending up to 72 hours with its charging case.
The U.S. pricing starts at $395 for Warby Parker models, while Gentle Monster frames range from $449 to $489.

articles.title: KSSP warns Mission Samudra threatens traditional fishing livelihoods
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demands curbs on Maritime Board’s sweeping powers; calls for protection of coastal commons and fragile marine ecosystems

The Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP) has urged the State government to reconsider Mission Samudra and the proposed Maritime Board Amendment Bill, warning that the initiatives could undermine traditional fishing livelihoods, facilitate corporate control over coastal resources and threaten fragile marine ecosystems.

In a statement, KSSP general secretary V. Manoj Kumar and president C. Ramakrishnan alleged that Mission Samudra, the State’s version of the Union government’s Blue Economy policy, sought to transform Keralam into a port-centric development hub through private participation.

The project envisages the development of 18 minor ports, improved connectivity with major ports such as Vizhinjam, Kochi and Vallarpadam, and the establishment of shipbuilding, repair and breaking facilities. Maritime tourism, a black sand corridor for mineral extraction and the development of Alappuzha as a Blue Economy hub are also proposed.

The parishad expressed concern that the proposed amendments would vest sweeping powers in the Maritime Board, including the creation of a land bank, a Port Area Development Authority and an enforcement wing with police-like powers. Its authority to acquire company shares and lease land for extended periods could turn the board into an instrument for transferring coastal resources to private interests, the signatories warned.

Pointing out that beaches are the principal workplaces of traditional fisherfolk in Keralam’s 222 marine fishing villages, the KSSP said the proposed legislation could undermine their customary rights over these common spaces used for landing catches, marketing fish, storing boats and nets, and drying fish.

It also criticised the project for failing to address the sustainability of Kerala’s annual marine fish catch of around six lakh tonnes or assess the ecological impact of large-scale coastal construction.

The parishad demanded participatory coastal-use mapping, legal protection of traditional fishing rights and safeguards against displacement. It also called for beach restoration, environmentally sustainable port development, protection of traditional fishing routes, and safe housing for coastal communities in the face of climate change.

Further, it demanded that coastal tourism initiatives incorporate fisherfolk through models such as pesca tourism and that Mission Samudra projects receive the consent of local self-government institutions.
The KSSP urged the government to ensure that coastal development does not come at the expense of fishing communities’ livelihoods, customary rights and environmental security.

articles.title: KPSC ‘recruitment scam’: ED attaches properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to former chairman, member and IAS officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The three officials allegedly abused their official positions to collect illegal gratification from candidates in exchange for assured selection through question paper leaks, supply of candidate-specific answer keys and manipulation of confidential marks during the preparation of the 1:3 eligibility list

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has provisionally attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to three former senior functionaries of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC ) in connection with the veterinary officer recruitment scam.

Those whose properties have been attached include former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar , commission member Geetha B.V. Shivamurthy and IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar , who was then Controller of Examinations.
The attachment order was issued on Friday (November 13) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

According to the ED investigation, the three officials allegedly abused their official positions in conspiracy with Basavaraj Kannale, a middleman, and others in order to collect illegal gratification from candidates in exchange for assured selection through question paper leaks, supply of candidate-specific answer keys and manipulation of confidential marks during preparation of the 1:3 eligibility list.

The investigation revealed that Mr. Gangwar allegedly leaked question papers, with the correct answers marked, to his close associate, Mr. Kannale, on January 7, 2026, the ED said. Mr. Kannale allegedly circulated the papers among 10 candidates at villas on the outskirts of Bengaluru on January 8, a day before the examination.

He reportedly demanded bribes ranging from ₹20 lakh to ₹40 lakh from candidates. A portion of the money was allegedly collected in advance, while the remaining amounts were secured through blank signed cheques and promissory notes.

The ED claimed that the OMR answer sheets of these candidates matched the initial answer key published by the KPSC, including answers that were subsequently declared incorrect in the revised answer key.

In another instance, at the alleged insistence of Mr. Sahukar, Mr. Gangwar allegedly used confidential seating arrangements and jumbled charts, which were under his custody, to prepare correct answers to 80 questions for six candidates.

The registration numbers of these candidates were allegedly provided by Ms. Geetha on January 8, and the answers were handed over to her. In return, the then chairman allegedly assured Mr. Gangwar of favourable interview marks in the KAS examination for a candidate of his choice.

The ED also seized a notebook from Mr. Sahukar’s residence containing centre-wise registration numbers of candidates, allegedly written in his handwriting. Mr. Sahukar allegedly collected ₹10 lakh in cash from one candidate against a deal of ₹20 lakh, while Ms. Geetha allegedly collected ₹20 lakh from another candidate against a deal of ₹40 lakh.

articles.title: Palnadu SP directs police personnel to remain vigilant ahead of municipal elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inspecting arrangements at nomination centres in the Narasaraopet Municipal Office, Jagadish Adahalli calls for smooth and peaceful conduct of nomination process

Palnadu Superintendent of Police (SP) Jagadish Adahalli on Saturday inspected the security arrangements at nomination centres established at the Narasaraopet Municipal Office ahead of the municipal elections.

During his visit, the SP reviewed the security measures and instructed police personnel on duty to remain vigilant and ensure that the nomination process was conducted peacefully and smoothly, without any untoward incidents.

He directed officials to provide adequate police security at all nomination centres and ensure strict compliance with election guidelines. Assuring candidates of adequate protection, Mr. Adahalli said they could visit the centres freely and file their nominations without fear or apprehension.

articles.title: Mass awareness rally held in Mysuru against drug abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Campaign under NALSA initiative focuses on protecting students and youth from substance abuse

Emphasising the need to protect young people from substance abuse, First Additional District and Sessions Judge Sandhya Rao P. called upon the youth to stay away from addictive substances and adopt a healthy lifestyle.
She was speaking after inaugurating an awareness rally against drug abuse organised under the NALSA’s DAWN (Drug Awareness and Wellness Navigation) initiative in Mysuru.

The programme was jointly organised by the District Legal Services Authority, Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Department of Justice, Mysuru Bar Association, Police Department and JSS Law College (Autonomous), along with other departments and organisations.

Ms. Rao said the primary objective of the campaign was to protect students and the younger generation from the harmful effects of narcotic substances. The youth were the future of the country and should not fall prey to addiction under any circumstances, she said.
The campaign sought to create awareness, particularly among children in the 12-18 age group and students, about the dangers of drug abuse.

The rally began at JSS Law College and passed through prominent junctions before culminating near the Old Court Complex, where floral tributes were paid to the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. Students raised slogans against drug abuse and carried placards highlighting its harmful consequences.

Senior Civil Judge and Member-Secretary of the District Legal Services Authority Nagaraj Siddappa Ankasadoddi, Additional Superintendent of Police Mallik C., Central Prison Chief Superintendent Sheshumurthy V., Deputy Director of the Department of Women and Child Development R. Nagaraj, Bar Association president S. Lokesh, JSS Law College Chief Executive K.S. Suresh and principal N. Vanishree were present.
Officials from various departments, doctors, panel advocates, college students and practitioners of the Heartfulness Institute also participated.

articles.title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12, say witnesses
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions

A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening (November 13, 2026) in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of state capital Sittwe.

"All I saw was their bodies scattered in pain. I could not find words to describe it. And we were lost with crying," she said. "It has broken our family. There were no others except my family. We did not hear the sound of the fighter jet — it just came and dropped the bombs."
Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions that have long held sway in the nation's fringes.

The western coastal state of Rakhine is among the regions worst hit by the war. Controlled almost entirely by the ethnic minority Arakan Army (AA), it has been blockaded by the military and pummelled with regular airstrikes. It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the latest attack.

Chit Su Wai said 12 people died in Friday's attack, a toll confirmed by Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, a rescue and emergency service. Khine Hein Htet said a five-year-old was among the dead, while 18 were also injured in the camp, where many residents had been living for four years.

"They believed the camp was safe, and they sheltered there together. When we arrived at the scene, most of the victims had died in one place," the 24-year-old said. He said it was not a combat area, adding: "We never thought this camp would be targeted."

The village was a mess of collapsed bamboo houses on Saturday, the wreckage of an upturned vehicle mixed among the debris of household goods and clothes. Locals had already removed the bodies, wrapping them in yellow and red plastic and burying them in makeshift graves.

Aung Kyaw Min, a 45-year-old tuktuk driver, described how he rushed to the village where his brother and sister lived after hearing of the attack. "My sister's body was already headless while my brother was lying dead," he said, crying.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had rejected a ceasefire on energy targets at talks in Abu Dhabi, as Moscow was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign

Mr. Zelensky said Russia was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign in its war with Ukraine, while warning that the Kremlin’s demands to redraw Europe’s security architecture were “dangerous” and could lead to more wars.

Mr. Zelensky spoke to the media on Friday (November 13, 2026), after visits to Denmark and Ireland, where he met European leaders following two days of U.S.-brokered Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi. The talks ended with no breakthrough in Europe’s worst war since the Second World War, but all sides agreed that European officials should be included in future negotiations.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff attended the Abu Dhabi talks, and then met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Mr. Zelensky separately.
Moscow turned down a proposal for a ceasefire in attacks on energy targets at the Abu Dhabi talks, Mr. Zelensky said. “On the proposal for an energy ceasefire: the Russians don’t want it,” he said.

He said Mr. Putin’s proposal for a “humanitarian mission” to Kostiantynivka was a ploy to get Kyiv to withdraw from the embattled city and open the road to more settlements in the Donetsk region. “Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city that way,” he said. Russia said this year that it had seized the town, but Ukraine has said fighting is continuing.

Moscow’s troops have inched westwards since launching the invasion in February 2022, but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Mr. Zelensky said the EU and NATO are Europe’s “only real security”, and that Moscow’s bid to review the continent’s security was “dangerous because... it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations.”

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Why have the U.S., Canada, Australia and Pakistan brought up allegations that the agency has spearheaded targeted killings and surveillance of separatists on their soil? What is the Indian government’s stand? Do these operations follow certain norms, especially if it’s a friendly country?

articles.title: Indian Railways to connect Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya through weekly train service
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations
Indian Railways is going to operate a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.

The Ministry of Railways stated in a statement on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the initiative is to link two places which are associated with “the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace Lord Ram.”
The route will cover approximately 604 kilometres, connecting Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.
Railways Ministry said that the service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.

Citing the role of railway connectivity on bilateral cooperation, the Ministry said in a statement, “India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.”
India and Nepal have held discussions on cross-border railway links, including passenger train services on the Janakpur-Ayodhya section, and bilateral cooperation in the sector in June this year.

articles.title: U.S. media names Indian official who allegedly ordered plot on Gurpatwant Singh Pannun
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

U.S. authorities believe the alleged plot to kill Khalistani activist, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, who is wanted on terror charges in India, was ordered by the previous chief of the Indian Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), and had official sanction from senior intelligence officials with “with ties to [Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inner circle”, the Washington Post, a U.S.-national daily, reported .

The report in the Washington Post newspaper identified, for the first time, an R&AW officer whose name had been withheld in the case papers made available by the Justice Department in New York in November 2023. In a separate press release, the Post said, on the basis of interviews with “more than three dozen current and former senior officials in the United States, India, Canada, Britain, Germany and Australia”, that other R&AW officers have faced “arrest, expulsion and reprimand” in recent months, indicating that there was more international coordination about what it called “escalating campaign of aggression” against Indian diaspora members by India’s intelligence operatives.

The Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the latest story in the Washington Post report on Monday. Last week, in response to a question on the allegations, the MEA spokesperson said that a “high-level committee is looking into information that was shared by the American side with us, because [it] also equally impacts our national security. In recent weeks, the government has also blocked the broadcast of documentaries by Canadian and Australian public broadcasters CBC and ABC that focussed on the allegations against Indian agencies for targeting Khalistani activists abroad.

“In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence officials have assessed that the operation targeting Pannun was approved by the RAW chief at the time, Samant Goel,” said the report. “U.S. spy agencies have more tentatively assessed that Mr. Modi’s National Security Adviser, Ajit Doval, was probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists,” it added.

According to the story, the R&AW official identified as Vikash Yadav had directed Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic pending extradition to the U.S. to stand trial in the case, to hire a hitman to kill GS Pannun outside his New York residence. Mr. Yadav, believed to be a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) official on deputation to the R&AW, has subsequently been repatriated to the paramilitary forces, other U.S. media have reported.

While the MEA Ministry of External Affairs has maintained that such killings are not Indian policy, and has denied Canadian allegations of a similar hit on Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, the government has agreed to an enquiry on the U.S. allegations.
The Washington Post story also dwells at length on differences between the U.S. White House administration and the Justice Department that oversaw the FBI-DEA investigation in the case.

The evidence cited had included an undercover American agent who was hired for the Pannun killing by Mr. Gupta, under direct orders from Mr. Yadav, surveillance of messages purportedly exchanged between them, as well as a photograph allegedly showing three Indian intelligence officials who gave the green signal for the plot during a video-call.

However, the report stated while the Justice Department pushed for an indictment against both Mr. Gupta and Mr. Yadav, Biden administration officials prevailed in ensuring the indictment is against only Mr. Gupta at present, ostensibly so as not to “rupture” ties with India.

The matter was thrashed out a series of meetings which included U.S. Deputy NSA Jon Finer, U.S. Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Deputy CIA Director David Cohen, the report said. It also stated Mr. President Biden had discussed the issue with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting in September 2023, calling for accountability for the case.

According to Washington Post, R&AW official Vikash Yadav directed businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic, to hire a hitman to kill Pannun outside his New York residence; it says NSA Ajit Doval was ‘probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists’

U.S. authorities believe the alleged plot to kill Khalistani activist, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, who is wanted on terror charges in India, was ordered by the previous chief of the Indian Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), and had official sanction from senior intelligence officials with “with ties to [Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inner circle”, the Washington Post, a U.S.-national daily, reported .

The report in the Washington Post newspaper identified, for the first time, an R&AW officer whose name had been withheld in the case papers made available by the Justice Department in New York in November 2023. In a separate press release, the Post said, on the basis of interviews with “more than three dozen current and former senior officials in the United States, India, Canada, Britain, Germany and Australia”, that other R&AW officers have faced “arrest, expulsion and reprimand” in recent months, indicating that there was more international coordination about what it called “escalating campaign of aggression” against Indian diaspora members by India’s intelligence operatives.

The Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the latest story in the Washington Post report on Monday. Last week, in response to a question on the allegations, the MEA spokesperson said that a “high-level committee is looking into information that was shared by the American side with us, because [it] also equally impacts our national security. In recent weeks, the government has also blocked the broadcast of documentaries by Canadian and Australian public broadcasters CBC and ABC that focussed on the allegations against Indian agencies for targeting Khalistani activists abroad.

“In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence officials have assessed that the operation targeting Pannun was approved by the RAW chief at the time, Samant Goel,” said the report. “U.S. spy agencies have more tentatively assessed that Mr. Modi’s National Security Adviser, Ajit Doval, was probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists,” it added.

According to the story, the R&AW official identified as Vikash Yadav had directed Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic pending extradition to the U.S. to stand trial in the case, to hire a hitman to kill GS Pannun outside his New York residence. Mr. Yadav, believed to be a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) official on deputation to the R&AW, has subsequently been repatriated to the paramilitary forces, other U.S. media have reported.

While the MEA Ministry of External Affairs has maintained that such killings are not Indian policy, and has denied Canadian allegations of a similar hit on Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, the government has agreed to an enquiry on the U.S. allegations.

The Washington Post story also dwells at length on differences between the U.S. White House administration and the Justice Department that oversaw the FBI-DEA investigation in the case.

The evidence cited had included an undercover American agent who was hired for the Pannun killing by Mr. Gupta, under direct orders from Mr. Yadav, surveillance of messages purportedly exchanged between them, as well as a photograph allegedly showing three Indian intelligence officials who gave the green signal for the plot during a video-call.

However, the report stated while the Justice Department pushed for an indictment against both Mr. Gupta and Mr. Yadav, Biden administration officials prevailed in ensuring the indictment is against only Mr. Gupta at present, ostensibly so as not to “rupture” ties with India.

The matter was thrashed out a series of meetings which included U.S. Deputy NSA Jon Finer, U.S. Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Deputy CIA Director David Cohen, the report said. It also stated Mr. President Biden had discussed the issue with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting in September 2023, calling for accountability for the case.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: ‘Abki baar, AQI 400-paar’: Congress takes a swipe at Modi over Delhi pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Jairam Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult

The Congress on Saturday (November 14, 2026) took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 2024 Lok Sabha election slogan, “Abki baar, 400-paar”, saying it had come true in the national capital, with Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) crossing the 400-mark.
In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!”

Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said.
“Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said.
Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Avian influenza confirmed in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore; over 1,500 chickens culled
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1) has been confirmed in chicken samples collected from a poultry farm at Kattiyankuppam village in Kurinjipadi taluk of Cuddalore district.

“The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, had confirmed the H5N1 avian influenza virus in samples collected from a poultry carcass on November 5, 2026,” District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar told The Hindu .

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre.

According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.”
He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.”

As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai.
On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said.
Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease.

“Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.

fullParagraphs: The ‌technology giant said it was “monitoring the backlog of email messages ‌accrued during this ​event” before considering the issue with ⁠the enterprise services resolved.
Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.
“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.
Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.
The Redmond, Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.
It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

Microsoft said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that services were fully restored after a massive outage that lasted for hours.

“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the company said in an update on X.

Users reported that Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

The outage affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks in many places. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had impacted some of their operations.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft said on its website. Problems started appearing around midday Thursday in the U.S.

The Redmond, Washington-based company apologised on Friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents.

It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” following a recent network change.

articles.title: Tirumala electric bus drivers stage protest demanding wage hike
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The APSRTC Electric Hired Bus Drivers and Workers’ Union, affiliated with the CITU, staged a dharna in front of the Alipiri depot in Tirupati on Saturday, demanding an immediate wage hike and an end to alleged harassment by the management.
More than 100 drivers took part in the protest, resulting in around 80 electric buses scheduled to operate between Tirupati and Tirumala remaining off the road.

CITU district honorary president G. Balasubrahmanyam, president S. Jayachandra and general secretary T. Subrahmanyam expressed solidarity with the protesters. They said the drivers played a crucial role in transporting thousands of devotees safely to Tirumala every day but were being paid meagre wages and denied duty assignments.

The CITU leaders alleged that an individual named Shamsher was harassing workers through his high-handed behaviour. Despite 17 rounds of talks and repeated representations to the Labour Department, the management had failed to resolve their grievances, they said. They also condemned the dismissal of 12 workers despite assurances that their issues would be addressed and demanded their immediate reinstatement.

The union also sought monthly payslips, identity cards, uniforms, rest rooms, timely ESI and PF contributions, double wages for double-duty shifts, weekly holidays, and night-out and ghat road allowances.

articles.title: Footwear hanging from trees marks a unique annual festival at Lakamma Devi temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Footwear hanging from trees is an unusual sight one encounters outside the Lakamma Devi temple at Gola (B) village, about 15 km from Kalaburagi, during its annual fair. For devotees, however, the sight is a symbol of faith, gratitude and fulfilled prayers.

Hundreds of devotees from Kalaburagi and neighbouring districts converged on the village on Saturday to take part in the two-day annual festival of Lakamma Devi, celebrated for its distinctive customs and rituals.

Observed on the sixth day after Deepavali, the annual jatra festival draws people cutting across caste and community barriers. Devotees visit the temple with prayers and seek the blessings of the deity. Those whose wishes are fulfilled return to offer footwear, which is tied into garlands and hung from trees outside the temple as an expression of gratitude.
The ritual lends the temple surroundings an unusual appearance, with footwear of different sizes and designs dangling from the branches, bearing testimony to the faith of devotees and their prayers.

The temple itself has a distinctive tradition. Devotees worship the posterior of the goddess, while saris are also offered and tied to the capstone of the shrine. Offerings to the deity include both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes, reflecting the unique customs associated with the annual fair.
For many devotees, the festival is not merely a religious gathering but an enduring tradition rooted in generations of faith.

Heerabai Naganalli and Kishore Benekal, devotees from Kalaburagi who have been attending the annual jatra for decades, said they firmly believed that Lakamma Devi protected her devotees from evil and helped relieve them of health-related problems.
They said the offering of footwear and sarees was an expression of gratitude for the fulfilment of prayers and the protection they believed the goddess bestowed upon them.
